## Summary
Qisda Corporation was founded on 21 April 1984 within the Acer group, launched the BenQ brand in December 2001 after the brand was spun off from Acer, and took the Qisda name in 2007 when the brand business was separated as BenQ Corporation [1][2]. It is headquartered in Taoyuan, Taiwan, employs more than 10,000 people, trades as TWSE 2352, and is an ODM/OEM whose lines span LCD displays, all-in-one computers, projectors, multifunction office devices, medical electronics, automotive electronics and networking products [1]. BenQ, today a Qisda subsidiary, sells monitors, projectors and interactive displays and sold BenQ-Siemens phones from 2005 until leaving the mobile market by 2015 [2]. Qisda holds seven IEEE MA-L blocks in the registry copy consulted (00:03:9D, 00:17:CA, 00:1E:21, 1C:E1:92, 64:E2:20, C0:C4:F9, D0:76:0C), all at its Taoyuan address [3]. As an ODM, a device carrying a Qisda OUI is most likely sold under another brand - this is an inference from its business model [1], not a documented mapping - and no source reached in this session states which product lines, radios or chipsets carry these blocks, so those fields are left unknown rather than guessed. No FCC grantee code, teardown or vendor security advisory was reachable either.
